report_name: Microsoft Teams Vishing Campaign by STAC4749 Deploys Chaos Ransomware

threat_actors.name: STAC4749
threat_actors.description: A threat actor tracked by Sophos that conducted a voice phishing (vishing) campaign using Microsoft Teams to deploy Chaos ransomware against North American organizations between February and June 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: The STAC4749 threat actor used Microsoft Teams calls to conduct voice phishing (vishing), posing as IT support staff to socially engineer employees into granting remote access.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The attackers convinced employees to grant them remote access to their machines, likely using a legitimate remote administration tool as part of a social engineering scheme.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: PowerShell was likely used by the attackers to download and execute the next stage payload after gaining initial access from the user's endpoint.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Chaos ransomware variant was deployed by STAC4749 to encrypt files across the compromised network, representing the final impact of the attack.

malware.name: Chaos
malware.description: A ransomware variant deployed by STAC4749 to encrypt files on compromised networks after gaining access via a vishing campaign.

malware.name: Custom Backdoor (STAC4749)
malware.description: A custom backdoor deployed by STAC4749 as part of its modular post-exploitation toolkit to establish a persistent command-and-control (C2) channel.

tools.name: Microsoft Teams
tools.description: Abused by the STAC4749 threat actor to conduct a voice phishing (vishing) campaign, initiating calls with employees to socially engineer them into granting remote access.

identities.name: North American Organizations
identities.description: Dozens of organizations across North America targeted by the STAC4749 vishing campaign between February and June 2026.

infrastructure.name: STAC4749 C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Unknown command-and-control infrastructure used by the custom backdoor to maintain persistence on compromised endpoints.

infrastructure.name: STAC4749 Social Engineering Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Fake cloud domains and personas created by STAC4749 to appear as legitimate IT or helpdesk support during the vishing campaign.

indicators.name: Suspicious Process Spawned by Microsoft Teams
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Process Spawned by Microsoft Teams
id: 5e8a1b9c-4f2d-4e8a-a9b1-c7d6e5f4a3b2
status: experimental
description: Detects command-line interpreters such as powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or cscript.exe being spawned as a child process of Teams.exe. This is highly anomalous and may indicate a vishing or social engineering attempt as seen in the STAC4749 campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/weekly-recap-rogue-ai-models-88m.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Teams.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects command-line interpreters being spawned as children of Teams.exe, which is highly anomalous and indicative of social engineering success.

indicators.name: Anomalous Microsoft Teams Communication from External Tenant
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Microsoft Teams Communication from External Tenant
id: 9d8c7b6a-5e4d-4c3b-a2a1-b0c9d8e7f6a5
status: experimental
description: Detects the addition of an external user to a Microsoft Teams channel. This is often a precursor to vishing campaigns like the one conducted by STAC4749, where attackers initiate contact from external tenants. This rule should be tuned based on organizational communication patterns.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/weekly-recap-rogue-ai-models-88m.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1566.004
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.teams
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'MemberAdded'
    Members|contains: '#EXT#'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a pattern of unsolicited calls or messages from external tenants to multiple users, which could indicate a vishing campaign.
